predecessors.name: Iraqi Republic
predecessors.text: the three governorates of Erbil, Sulaymaniyah and Duhok; 'Iraqi troops were withdrawn from the Kurdish regions in October 1991' (Operation Provide Comfort page)

ledger.x: 19 May 1992: the Kurdistan Region holds its first elections.
15 October 2005: the Region becomes a federal region of Iraq.
June 2014: the Peshmerga take the disputed areas.
15-16 October 2017: Iraq moves on the disputed territories.
17 October 2017: Khanaqin, Jalawla, Bashiqa and Sinjar.

wars.name: Iraqi Kurdish Civil War
wars.outcome: May 1994 to November 1997 (KDP unilateral ceasefire 24 November 1997): the KDP, dominant in Erbil and Dohuk, and the PUK, dominant in Sulaymaniyah and Halabja, fought over towns inside the Region (Shaqlawa, Chamchamal); 30,000 Iraqi troops took Erbil on 31…

wars.name: 2017 Iraqi-Kurdish conflict
wars.outcome: 15-31 October 2017: Iraq retook Kirkuk (16 October), Khanaqin, Jalawla, Bashiqa and Sinjar (17 October) and the Mosul Dam (18 October); fighting at Zummar on 26 October; the Region lost 40% (or 'a fifth') of the land it administered.

wars.name: War in Iraq (2013-2017): Kurdish front
wars.outcome: ISIL took Sinjar in early August 2014 after the Peshmerga abandoned it; the Peshmerga offensive of 17 December 2014 ended with Sinjar retaken on 13 November 2015.

certainty.note: The Region's line is a de facto military line from October 1991, called 'the Green Line' without definition on the page; the disputed territories 'remain contested' between Erbil and Baghdad.
